candidates.role: document-assembly engine candidate — measured on our corpus (#15); implementation target doc.marker (#16)
candidates.evidence: 2026-07-23 run over 20 scanned image-only exam PDFs (~100 pages; math + tables + multi-column), fully on-machine, --mode balanced, surya-2 GGUF served by llama-server: text OCR and inline-math LaTeX produced cleanly (best math of the three engines compared); reading order degraded — page headers/footers interleave mid-question
candidates.caveats: APPLE-SILICON LAYOUT FRAGILITY: surya-2 sends response_format json_schema for its layout/table models, which llama-server must convert to GBNF. brew build 9960 aborted the whole run ('Failed to initialize samplers: failed to parse grammar' → health-check failure, no output); build 10090 completes but the layout/table grammar still fails (~20 errors/doc), so assembly — marker's signature capability — is the casualty on this path. Text + inline-math survive because they go through the recognition VLM, not the grammar path. Upgrading llama.cpp is the right first step but not a fix: its structured-output path is weaker than vllm's. Estimand note: the T2 claim here is qualitative fidelity on our corpus, NOT a benchmark score — do not mix with surya's vendor olmOCR-bench number

candidates.role: potential first-party bestOCR engine — same shape as the existing Ollama VLM builds (llm + mmproj GGUF)
candidates.evidence: vendor self-reported olmOCR-bench 83.3; we have only ever exercised surya-2 wrapped inside marker, never measured it standalone on our corpus
candidates.caveats: T3 is deliberate: our #15 evidence is about MARKER's behaviour, not surya's own accuracy — attributing marker's results to surya would be a cross-estimand error. Admitting surya as a bestOCR engine would need its own smoke-test + sweep to earn T2. Apache-2.0 code and weights (unlike chandra, whose OpenRAIL-M weights make it cloud-reference-tier only). PIN DECISION (#29): ext.surya deliberately stays on the 0.17.x classical generation (self-contained, no model server — the fallback that survives llama-server breakage); this entry is what admitting surya-2 as a SEPARATE engine would build on, not an upgrade path for ext.surya

candidates.model: PaddleOCR document pipeline (PP-DocLayoutV2 layout detection → crop → VL recognition → assemble)
candidates.role: document-assembly engine candidate — measured on our corpus (#15); implementation target doc.paddleocr-pipeline (#16)
candidates.evidence: 2026-07-23 3-way comparison on the same scanned multiple-choice stats page (paddleocr 3.7.0 / paddle 3.3.1, CPU on Apple Silicon): reading order CORRECT — header stays at top, Q1-Q6 in order, no interleaving. Best reading order of the three engines compared
candidates.caveats: DISTINCT FROM the 'PaddleOCR-VL-1.6' entry above and from the classical 'PP-OCRv5 / PP-StructureV3' entry — three different Paddle things with three different estimands: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 is per-page ELEMENT recognition (the GGUF we run in Ollama), PP-OCRv5/StructureV3 is the classical non-LLM det+rec pipeline, and THIS is the document-assembly pipeline. Never merge their numbers. Own quirk: mis-classified the whole multiple-choice block as one <table> (each line a row). No LaTeX (HTML-wrapped text). Runs paddle CPU on Apple Silicon (no MPS) — local-capable but slower than the Ollama/llama.cpp per-page path; heavier install (paddleocr + paddlepaddle + paddlex[ocr]). Architectural reason it beats marker here: PP-DocLayout is a dedicated DETECTION model, not a grammar-constrained VLM call, so it sidesteps the llama.cpp json_schema→GBNF fragility entirely — this is the '#15 design constraint: keep layout out of the grammar path'
